trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Bareilly - Case No.1123 of 2005
case_name: Smt. Usha & Others vs Mahendra Pal Singh & Another
facts_of_case: Usha filed an application under section 125 Cr.P.C. for maintenance allowance of her children with the allegation that she was married to Mahendra Pal Singh and they had three children. The marriage was dissolved under section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act. Usha claimed Rs.3000/- per month as maintenance allowance for each child, while Mahendra Pal Singh alleged that he was unemployed and earning only Rs.1200/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: The right of a minor girl for maintenance from parents after attaining majority till her marriage under section 20(3) of Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act survives.
legal_principles.held: The right of a minor girl for maintenance from parents after attaining majority till her marriage under section 20(3) of Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act survives.

legal_principles.principle: An unmarried major daughter is not entitled to get the maintenance allowance under section 125 Cr.P.C. unless she proves further that she is unable to maintain herself and such inability is attributable to physical or mental abnormality or injury.
legal_principles.held: She has to prove further that she is unable to maintain herself and such inability to maintain herself is attributable to physical or mental abnormality or injury, if any, she is afflicted with.
keywords: physical or mental abnormality or injury

outcome.final_order: Maintenance allowance of Rs.500/- per month awarded to Umang with effect from the date of the order, while maintenance allowance of Km. Sakshi and Km. Nishtha was dismissed as they were majors.
